description: List the footnotes an article cites — its reference lists, in document order — with each footnote's text, external links (archive copies included), and DOIs. wikipedia_get_article drops footnote markers and reference lists, so use this for the sources behind a claim. label is the in-text marker without brackets; group names a notes list such as "lower-alpha" and is absent for the main list. A short citation such as "Galinsky 2012, pp. 75–76" carries work_ids, and works on the same page holds the full citations they name, each once. Pages hold limit whole footnotes; each page repeats the full-article parse, so read the whole list in as few pages as it allows by passing a limit up to total_references (at most 500 per page). Follow next_cursor as cursor with the same title and language to continue at the same revision. Bibliography and further-reading entries no footnote points to are not listed — read those sections with wikipedia_get_article. Redirects are followed; the revision_id and url cite the article read.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the previous page. Keep title and language unchanged. The cursor carries no variant, so pass variant on every page it should convert. Empty means the first page.

limit.description: Footnotes per page (default 25). Positive integers above 500 are clamped with a notice. Each call's limit sizes its own page, so it may change between pages.

title.description: Article title (e.g. "Seine"). A trailing #fragment is accepted and ignored; the characters < > [ ] { } and | cannot appear in a Wikipedia page name. Special: and Media: titles, and interwiki links such as "wikt:cat", name no page.

variant.description: Script variant to convert the returned text to, on an edition with a language converter: "zh-hans", "zh-hant", "zh-cn", or "zh-tw" on zh; "sr-ec" (Cyrillic) or "sr-el" (Latin) on sr; "uz-latn" or "uz-cyrl" on uz. Pass the edition as language and the variant here. Matched case-insensitively against the edition's own list; an edition without a converter, such as en, accepts none. Omit it, or pass "", to read the text as stored. title and the other identifiers stay as stored, so title still chains into other calls.

name: wikipedia_get_references

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `not_found`: No Wikipedia article exists for the given title, or the title is blank. `invalid_title`: The title can name no page: it contains characters MediaWiki forbids in a page name, is a Special: or Media: title in any edition's spelling, or is an interwiki link such as "wikt:cat". `invalid_language`: The language is not a valid BCP 47 code, or names a Wikipedia edition that does not exist. `invalid_variant`: The variant is not one the language edition converts to, or the edition has no script variants. `invalid_cursor`: The cursor is malformed, was issued for another title or language, or points past the last footnote. `revision_unavailable`: The revision the cursor is pinned to no longer exists, is hidden, or cannot be read or verified. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

next_cursor.description: Pass unchanged as cursor with the same title and language for the next page. Absent on the last page.

notice.description: Where to look instead when the article has no footnotes, or that limit was clamped.

pageid.description: Wikipedia page ID. Absent on API parse responses that omit it.

redirect_section.description: Section the alias points into, as the redirect's raw fragment names it. The footnotes listed are still the whole article's.

redirected_from.description: Original alias followed to the resolved article.

references.description: Footnotes on this page, in document order. Empty when the article has none.

group.description: Notes group the footnote belongs to (e.g. "lower-alpha", "N"). Absent for the main reference list.

label.description: In-text marker without brackets (e.g. "2", "a", "N 1"). Absent when no marker in the article links to the footnote.

text.description: Footnote text as plain text. Markers of other footnotes inside it are kept as [label].

urls.description: Every external link in the footnote, verbatim, archive copies included.

work_ids.description: CITEREF anchors a short citation links to. The citations they name are in works on the same page.

revision_id.description: ID of the revision the footnotes were read from. Every page of one read carries the same revision.

totalCount.description: Footnotes in the article across every reference list — total_references.

total_references.description: Footnotes in the article across every reference list, on all pages.

url.description: Canonical desktop URL of the article (e.g. "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine"), for citing the page.

variant.description: Script variant the text was converted to, spelled as the edition lists it ("zh-cn" for "zh-CN"). Absent when no variant was requested.

works.description: Full citations the work_ids on this page resolve to, each once. A work_id with no matching anchor in the article has no entry.

id.description: CITEREF anchor id of the full citation (e.g. "CITEREFGalinsky2012").

urls.description: Every external link in the citation, verbatim, archive copies included.

title: Get Wikipedia References
